svg.aria-label: Diagram comparing what the default VPC flow log format records with what the later opt-in field versions add. On the left, the version 2 default: version, account id, interface id, source and destination address, source and destination port, protocol, packets, bytes, start, end, action and log status. It is enough to say that two addresses exchanged packets. On the right, the opt-in fields that answer investigation questions: packet-level source and destination address in version 3, which separate the original sender from an intermediate NAT gateway or EKS node; flow direction and traffic path in version 5; ECS task and container fields in version 7; reject reason in version 8; encryption status in version 10; and instance tags, interface type and next hop fields in version 11. Across the bottom, the accuracy caveats: metadata fields not taken from the packet header are best effort approximations that may be missing or inaccurate, a SKIPDATA log status means records were dropped for an internal capacity constraint, timestamps carry up to sixty seconds of slack, and no version contains payload, which is where Traffic Mirroring begins.
svg.title: The default flow log format is the version that answers the least, and the one you cannot change
svg.text: The fields arrived over nine versions. The default stayed at two.
And no field can be added backwards: a log written yesterday carries the decision you made before it.
“You cannot customize or change the default format.”
Enough to say that two addresses
Behind a NAT gateway or an EKS node,
every host looks like the same host.
Any number of fields, in any order, minimum one.
behind the hop. Also tcp-flags, instance-id.
eight egress paths it actually took.
ECS task, service and container fields.
Some need IAM permissions, or they write a dash.
What it is, in AWS's own words
• Metadata fields not taken from the packet header are “best effort approximations, and their values might be missing or inaccurate”.
• A log-status of SKIPDATA means records were dropped for an internal capacity constraint or error.
• start and end carry up to 60 seconds of slack in either direction. Delivery to S3 is typically ~10 minutes after a ~10 minute window.
No version of a flow log contains payload.
That is where Traffic Mirroring begins — captured at the network interface, which “cannot be disabled or tampered with from a user space”,
and billed per session-hour until the session is deleted, even after the source instance is stopped or terminated.
